unchanged: Stable journal_v3.py and all root tracked files.
Original journal index, transaction SQLite and event bytes; adoption adds only a persistent ownership fence, and prune may unlink bound original segment files after archive publication.

files.original: journal-index.json, transactions.sqlite3 and segment-NNNNNN.jsonl remain authoritative raw facts
files.fence: Original writer.lock is created exclusively after complete verification and contains exact manager nonce/store path/original index SHA. It is retained permanently to prevent stable reopen. A foreign, replaced or missing fence prevents complete managed reads.
files.manifest: External manifest.json: schema, nonce, source canonical path, originalIndexSha256, transaction binding, generation, archive binding, checkpoints, retained roots, segment locations, pending intent; checksum covers every field.
files.archive: One immutable full ZIP with exact original index/cache/segment members, duplicate/path/symlink/encryption/size/hash/member semantics verified before use. Archive path is outside source and manager.
files.operation: operation.lock is an exclusively created persistent lock carrying nonce/token; a nonblocking OS byte lock is held for the whole live operation or read lease. Abandoned locks need explicit recovery; they are never silently removed.
files.intent: prune-intent.json binds base/new manifest generations, original segment SHA/bytes/seq range, archive/index/checkpoint identities and retained-root digest before any unlink.

reader.input: Original source directory plus external manifest; source directory and its index/cache/ownership fence must remain present.
reader.view: Stream exact hot files and selected archive members into a new task-owned bounded temporary directory. Do not load the log into a list, rebase snapshots, replace original seq, or synthesize versions. Reuse raw JournalReader on this reconstructed immutable view, including its transaction-cache and lifecycle checks.
reader.markerRule: Check the ORIGINAL source writer.lock against the exact owned fence and reject journal-failure.json/journal-invalidated.json plus dangling symlinks/inspection errors before and after all stages and successful iterator termination. Temp-view validation never overrides original markers.
reader.references: Rebuild point source graph from actual reconstructed events. Every read/writer-predecessor reference must already have a factual same-key version source at observation. Unknown/active transactions, SQL/condition source proof gaps, unresolved version roots and unsupported models block prune and source-closed windows.
reader.delivery: A yielded prefix is diagnostic until the generator terminates and final original-marker/manifest/archive checks succeed. Read leases hold the OS operation lock and block prune/recovery.

apis.adopt: ManagedSource.adopt(store,source,model='point-register-v1',exclusive_source_ownership=True): complete sealed source only; acquire persistent original writer.lock before changing metadata. Failed adoption preserves the fence and/or operation lock, never unlocks uncertain evidence.
apis.archive: archive_checkpoint(name,new_zip): stream verified complete reconstructed raw source to new ZIP, fsync and reopen/semantically verify it, then publish its binding and checkpoint in a new manifest generation.
apis.pin: pin(name,transactions=(),versions=(),sequences=()): explicit bounded retained roots; complete recursive transaction/read/predecessor/initial closure stays hot. Source index references.versionSources are always included; active/unread refs reject adoption/prune.
apis.read: verify()/iter_events()/read_window(name): same original facts may be read from hot or archive. Original cold segments may be absent only when exact location entries already bind readable archive members.
apis.prune: prune(before_seq): original whole segments only, lastSeq<cutoff, all events outside recursive retained closure, no read lease, complete checkpoint/archive, immutable source epoch. No deletion of index/cache/fence/archive or arbitrary computed paths.
apis.recover: recover(expected_plan,exclusive_recovery=True): only explicit prepared plan and exact abandoned lock token, nonblocking OS lock proves no cooperative live owner. Reverify original fence/markers/archive/raw source/root generation before resuming remaining exact segment unlinks and finalizing; incomplete/foreign/ambiguous state remains locked and incomplete.
apis.archiveDeletion: Always refused in this slice. Retention of archive/checkpoint references is not relaxed.

pruneOrder: Verify original fence/markers/index/cache, archive members, full raw lifecycle and recursive retained roots.
Persist+fsync prepared prune intent with all bindings and root generation.
Publish+fsync new location manifest pointing eligible segments to archive before unlink.
For each exact original segment, recheck generation/markers/archive binding and current file SHA/size, then unlink and sync source directory where supported.
Reconstruct and verify all actual raw events through the new location map; retained roots and event count/seq/hash remain identical.
Publish finalized manifest and clear intent after durable verification; keep permanent source fence.
crashPolicy: Any unresolved intent or interrupted/failed operation blocks complete reads and new prune.
After intent but before manifest switch, old hot files remain; explicit recovery may proceed only with exact plan.
After manifest switch, any subset of target hot files may remain or be absent; all raw facts must still be available from verified archive.
Recovery never trusts a passed/verified boolean or cache alone and never repairs source facts from search/model output.
If marker persistence also fails, live instance remains permanently incomplete and the pre-existing operation lock is retained.

File fsync and atomic replacement are used. POSIX directory fsync is attempted; Windows stdlib directory power-loss durability is not proven, and process-fault tests must not be described as physical power-cut certification.
budgetRule: Every copy/hash/decompression stream charges IO bytes before retaining/copying blocks; raw JournalReader pass work is reserved conservatively from bound source/cache sizes. Graph/event traversals check record and cooperative wall budgets; temporary directory usage is checked before publication. A wall limit is cooperative, not an OS CPU quota. No formal performance or large-log throughput claim.
